title: They became best friends - then discovered they were brother and sister

evidence_packet.title: They became best friends - then discovered they were brother and sister
evidence_packet.lead: Andrea Urmston knew she had an adopted brother, only to discover he was already her closest friend
evidence_packet.summary: Andrea Urmston knew she had an adopted brother, only to discover he was already her closest friend
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Dave Green and Andrea Urmston found they instantly hit it off when their paths crossed while working in separate roles at Manchester Airport The two strangers got on so well they could complete each other's sentences - which made sense when they discovered the truth Dave was the adopted brother Andrea had not seen in more than 30 years "I was shaking, I was just shaking and my heart was pounding," Andrea told the BBC. "I'd finally found him. It's unbelievable." In 2005, Dave was managing the bus station at the airport and Andrea serviced the vending machines Over the next two years they became firm friends, texting and phoning each other when they were not at work

title: Burnham to spend first day working from No 10 North

evidence_packet.title: Burnham to spend first day working from No 10 North
evidence_packet.lead: Various ministers are also set to work regularly from the northern branch of Downing Street
evidence_packet.summary: Various ministers are also set to work regularly from the northern branch of Downing Street
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Burnham to spend first day working from No 10 North - BBC News Image source, PA Media By Jennifer McKiernan , Political reporter and Jack Fenwick, Political correspondent Published 23 July 2026 Updated 5 hours ago Andy Burnham will hold his first meeting at the new No 10 North in Manchester later on Friday. The branch of Downing Street in the North West will form part of the prime minister's aim to shift power from Whitehall and Westminster to regions across the country. Ministers Lucy Powell and Louise Haigh will also operate regularly from the new site, with up to 300 civil servants expected to join them by the end of next year. On Friday in Manchester Burnham will chair a meeting of the National Economic Council, a cabinet committee first launched in 2008 to respond to economic challenges around the UK. The meeting will bring together senior ministers and regional mayors to "put devolution at the centre of the government's mission to make Britain better". Ahead of that meeting, the prime minister said: "For 40 years, power and resources have been sucked into the centre, and too many communities have felt forgotten, without the attention and investment they deserve." He added: "The days of Whitehall resisting devolution are over, for good." Strategic decisions about devolution and local economic growth will shift from the Treasury and the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government to No 10 North, although both departments will have input in these areas. Angela Rayner, whose constituency is in Greater Manchester, is also expected to work from the new site for the first time on Friday. To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser. title: Man who drove at and killed boy riding stolen e-bike jailed

evidence_packet.title: Man who drove at and killed boy riding stolen e-bike jailed
evidence_packet.lead: Terrence King acted not in an "attempt to recover the bike but to get revenge or punish the boy"
evidence_packet.summary: Terrence King acted not in an "attempt to recover the bike but to get revenge or punish the boy"
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Man who drove at and killed boy riding stolen e-bike jailed - BBC News Image source, GMP Image caption, Terrence King was convicted following a two-week trial By Ewan Gawne North West Published 23 July 2026 A man who deliberately rammed his car into a teenage boy riding a stolen bike has been jailed for 16 years for murder. Terrence King drove into 15-year-old Devon Simmonds-Caines on Rowrah Crescent in Middleton, Greater Manchester on 22 July last year. The court heard Simmonds-Caines had stolen the £3,000 e-bike from another boy on the Langley Estate before he was pursued by King, who steered his vehicle into him. King, 60, who was found guilty after a two-week trial, was handed a 17-year sentence at Minshull Street Crown Court earlier. He had pleaded guilty to manslaughter but denied murder at the outset of the trial. Senior investigating officer Duncan Thorpe, of Greater Manchester Police, said King "deliberately drove his car into Devon" and caused the injuries that led to his death. Image source, GMP Image caption, Devon Simmonds-Caines, 15, died in Middleton in July 2025 In the trial, CCTV and doorbell camera footage showed Simmonds-Caines riding the e-bike, which the court heard he and a friend had stolen from another boy on the estate. There was a fracas and punches thrown before Devon rode off on the e-bike, the court heard. King drove at Devon Simmonds-Caines at about 11:55 BST on 22 July after chasing him following the reported theft. Prosecutors said it was not an "attempt to recover the bike but to get revenge or punish the boy". The boy was thrown into the air and died at the scene, GMP said. In a tribute issued after his death, Simmonds-Caines' family described him as a "bubbly person" who "only wanted the best for everyone around him" . Get in touch Tel

title: Friend of Manchester synagogue attacker jailed over separate plot on military base

evidence_packet.title: Friend of Manchester synagogue attacker jailed over separate plot on military base
evidence_packet.lead: Mohammad Bashir, 31, drove Jihad Al-Shamie on a trip to conduct hostile reconnaissance at a military base
evidence_packet.summary: Mohammad Bashir, 31, drove Jihad Al-Shamie on a trip to conduct hostile reconnaissance at a military base
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Friend of Manchester synagogue attacker jailed over separate plot on military base - BBC News Image source, Greater Manchester Police Image caption, Bashir was caught on CCTV discussing plans for an attack with Jihad Al-Shamie By Ewan Gawne and Rachael Lazaro , North West Published 23 July 2026 A man who planned an attack on a military base with the Manchester synagogue attacker has been jailed for life with a minimum term of 17 years. Mohammad Bashir, 31, drove his friend Jihad Al-Shamie on a 10-hour round trip to conduct hostile reconnaissance at the UK's Defence Academy in Shrivenham, Oxfordshire, on 14 August 2025. Weeks after that journey, Al-Shamie, 35, was shot dead by police after carrying out the Heaton Park Synagogue attack, in which two Jewish men were killed. Bashir, from Cheetham Hill, was sentenced at Manchester Crown Court after pleading guilty to one count of preparing an act of terrorism. Sentencing Bashir, Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb told him that by August last year he had become a "firmly committed jihadist". He and Al-Shamie were "equally engaged" in planning an attack on a British military target "in which you and he expected to kill and be killed", she said. She rejected his claim to a probation officer that he no longer held extremist views and regretted his actions. The judge said: "I consider you remain dangerous. You have given no grounds that your attitude has really changed at all." Following sentencing, Manchester-born Bashir, who also holds a Pakistani passport, smiled to family members in the upper public gallery of the courtroom as he walked from the dock. title: Three hurt as BB gun fired at Jewish people in Salford

evidence_packet.title: Three hurt as BB gun fired at Jewish people in Salford
evidence_packet.lead: The weapon was fired from a passing car on Leicester Road, in Salford, police say
evidence_packet.summary: The weapon was fired from a passing car on Leicester Road, in Salford, police say
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Three hurt as BB gun fired at Jewish people in Salford - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, Two people have been arrested on suspicion of religiously aggravated assault By Georgie Docker North West Published 23 July 2026 Three people have been injured after a BB gun was fired at Jewish people from a passing car in a suspected religiously aggravated attack. The victims, who were all adults, were shot on Leicester Road in Salford at about 22:00 BST on Monday and suffered minor injuries, Greater Manchester Police said. Two people have been arrested on suspicion of religiously aggravated common assault and remain in custody for questioning. The force said: "Threats to our communities will not be tolerated and we're continuing to enhance our security in Jewish communities across Greater Manchester to help keep them safe on our streets." title: Why voting method change matters in mayoral poll

evidence_packet.title: Why voting method change matters in mayoral poll
evidence_packet.lead: Why the Supplementary Vote may allow voters to vote with their heads and their hearts
evidence_packet.summary: Why the Supplementary Vote may allow voters to vote with their heads and their hearts
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Labour Party could benefit most from the return of the supplementary votes (SV) system in the Greater Manchester mayoral race, a polling expert has said Voters in the region head to the polls on 30 July and will be able to select a first and second choice of candidate as SV comes into replace the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system used at the last election A number of candidates have already declared for the contest , triggered after Andy Burnham's successful campaign to become the MP of Makerfield, leaving the post he has held since 2017 vacant Prof Jonathan Tonge of the University of Liverpool said Labour could pick up second preference votes from Greens and Lib Dems, while Reform could be less likely to see Restore voters put them as second preference due to "bad blood" between the party leaders The system was used in the first two mayoral elections, but was scrapped by the last Conservative government in favour of FPTP system, before it was reintroduced again by Labour Under SV, candidates need to win more than 50% of the vote in the first round to be come mayor or the top two candidates go into a run-off where second preference votes from eliminated candidates are counted

title: What is the Greater Manchester mayor and what do they do?

evidence_packet.title: What is the Greater Manchester mayor and what do they do?
evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester goes to the polls on 30 July, but what powers does the region's mayor hold?
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester goes to the polls on 30 July, but what powers does the region's mayor hold?
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham's victory in the Makerfield by-election means he has to step down as Greater Manchester mayor Burnham has been mayor since the role was first created in 2017 and the race to become his successor will be fiercely contested by all involved But what is the role they will be fighting for? The role of mayor was created as part of a law passed in 2016, one of a number of big pieces of devolution legislation brought in by the Conservatives after taking power in 2010 In a 2012 referendum, Manchester rejected having a directly-elected city mayor, along with eight other major cities, but the decision to have a regional or metropolitan mayor was directly negotiated between the government and the 10 Greater Manchester councils Andy Burnham, who left Parliament to stand for the role, was chosen as Labour's candidate for the first mayoral election in 2017 and won, taking 63.4% of the vote

title: Grooming gang victim from North West has convictions quashed

evidence_packet.title: Grooming gang victim from North West has convictions quashed
evidence_packet.lead: The woman was "in the grip of a groomer' when she was convicted at 14 of offences
evidence_packet.summary: The woman was "in the grip of a groomer' when she was convicted at 14 of offences
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Grooming gang victim from North West has convictions quashed - BBC News Image caption, The Commission said it has received other applications concerning grooming gangs, and it has a "body of in-house expertise" to help with them By Lynette Horsburgh North West Published 23 July 2026 The convictions of a woman who was groomed and sexually exploited as a child have been quashed. In 2002, at the age of 14, the woman referred to as Ms AB from the North West of England received a non-custodial sentence after being convicted of being carried in a stolen motor vehicle, possession of an imitation firearm and assault. The convictions have now been overturned after a referral by the Criminal Cases Review Commission (CCRC) which concluded there was a real possibility they would not be upheld because the prosecution, following her arrest by a police force not identified by the review, may have 'amounted to an abuse of process'. The CCRC's investigation found compelling evidence that, at the time of the offences, Ms AB had been the victim of child sexual exploitation and grooming. During an interview with the CCRC the woman explained how a man would bring food to her house, flatter her and make her feel special. Within months, the interactions with the man became sexual, and she was encouraged to have sex with his friends. She explained he would use violence and emotional blackmail to get her to comply. Image source, Criminal Cases Review Commission Image caption, CCRC chairwoman Dame Vera Baird said Ms AB was a "vulnerable child in need of protection" The CCRC referral followed publication of Baroness Louise Casey's National Audit on Group-based Child Sexual Exploitation and Abuse , external , which highlighted widespread institutional failings in protecting children from grooming

title: The Odyssey cast shown oldest book copy of Homer's epic poem

evidence_packet.title: The Odyssey cast shown oldest book copy of Homer's epic poem
evidence_packet.lead: Holding the oldest book copy of the text left director Christopher Nolan "very moved", a curator says
evidence_packet.summary: Holding the oldest book copy of the text left director Christopher Nolan "very moved", a curator says
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The task of taking parts of the oldest book copy of The Odyssey to the US for the stars of Christopher Nolan's cinematic retelling of the epic to view was "like being on the set of Mission Impossible", the librarian who took it has said Part of a 1,700-year-old copy of Homer's poem, kept at Manchester's John Rylands Library, was taken to New York in a bespoke case for the viewing Prof Christopher Pressler said it felt like a mission, as "we knew what was in this case but nobody else did", adding "It was a huge responsibility carrying something of global importance through JFK." He said it led to "some mind-blowing moments" for the cast, with Nolan being "very moved" by holding the fragments The fragments, written in ancient Greek by what was thought to be an Egyptian scribe and his teacher, are the oldest existing version of the poem arranged into a book Nolan's film, which was adapted from Homer's epic, stars Matt Damon as Odysseus, with Tom Holland playing his son, Telemachus, and Anne Hathaway as his wife, Penelope

title: Winter Hill still not fully recovered from moor fire eight years ago

evidence_packet.title: Winter Hill still not fully recovered from moor fire eight years ago
evidence_packet.lead: Winter Hill, near Bolton, is still recovering years after a wildfire, according to the Wildlife Trust
evidence_packet.summary: Winter Hill, near Bolton, is still recovering years after a wildfire, according to the Wildlife Trust
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A moorland hit by a devastating wildfire eight years ago has still not fully recovered The summer 2018 blaze on Winter Hill near Bolton lasted 42 days and took about 100 firefighters to control and put out While some of the landscape has recovered, Alan Wright, from The Wildlife Trust for Lancashire, Manchester and North Merseyside, said the impact was still visible He said: "The hill was completely black and this whole hill behind us was on fire. And it's not quite got the same kind of vegetation [now]." He added: "Any time there's a fire it will kill lots and lots of fledglings, it will kill lots of mammals, it will kill lots of insects, and then it will create areas which are just no-go areas for years to come because there are no food plants." Wright said that despite the long-term damage, a lot of work has been done to help re-grow plants and make the environment one in which wildlife could thrive again

evidence_packet.summary: The branch of Downing Street in the North West will form part of the prime minister's aim to shift power from Whitehall and Westminster to regions across the country Ministers Lucy Powell and Louise Haigh will also operate regularly from the new site, with up to 300 civil servant
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The branch of Downing Street in the North West will form part of the prime minister's aim to shift power from Whitehall and Westminster to regions across the country Ministers Lucy Powell and Louise Haigh will also operate regularly from the new site, with up to 300 civil servants expected to join them by the end of next year On Friday in Manchester Burnham will chair a meeting of the National Economic Council, a cabinet committee first launched in 2008 to respond to economic challenges around the UK The meeting will bring together senior ministers and regional mayors to "put devolution at the centre of the government's mission to make Britain better" Ahead of that meeting, the prime minister said: "For 40 years, power and resources have been sucked into the centre, and too many communities have felt forgotten, without the attention and investment they deserve." He added: "The days of Whitehall resisting devolution are over, for good."

title: Why voting method change matters in mayoral poll

evidence_packet.title: Why voting method change matters in mayoral poll
evidence_packet.lead: The Labour Party could benefit most from the return of the supplementary votes (SV) system in the Greater Manchester mayoral race, a polling expert has said Voters in the region head to the polls on 30 July and will be able to select a first and second choice of candidate as SV c
evidence_packet.summary: The Labour Party could benefit most from the return of the supplementary votes (SV) system in the Greater Manchester mayoral race, a polling expert has said Voters in the region head to the polls on 30 July and will be able to select a first and second choice of candidate as SV c
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Labour Party could benefit most from the return of the supplementary votes (SV) system in the Greater Manchester mayoral race, a polling expert has said Voters in the region head to the polls on 30 July and will be able to select a first and second choice of candidate as SV comes into replace the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system used at the last election A number of candidates have already declared for the contest , triggered after Andy Burnham's successful campaign to become the MP of Makerfield, leaving the post he has held since 2017 vacant Prof Jonathan Tonge of the University of Liverpool said Labour could pick up second preference votes from Greens and Lib Dems, while Reform could be less likely to see Restore voters put them as second preference due to "bad blood" between the party leaders The system was used in the first two mayoral elections, but was scrapped by the last Conservative government in favour of FPTP system, before it was reintroduced again by Labour Under SV, candidates need to win more than 50% of the vote in the first round to be come mayor or the top two candidates go into a run-off where second preference votes from eliminated candidates are counted

title: What is the Greater Manchester mayor and what do they do?

evidence_packet.title: What is the Greater Manchester mayor and what do they do?
evidence_packet.lead: Andy Burnham's victory in the Makerfield by-election means he has to step down as Greater Manchester mayor Burnham has been mayor since the role was first created in 2017 and the race to become his successor will be fiercely contested by all involved But what is the role they wil
evidence_packet.summary: Andy Burnham's victory in the Makerfield by-election means he has to step down as Greater Manchester mayor Burnham has been mayor since the role was first created in 2017 and the race to become his successor will be fiercely contested by all involved But what is the role they wil
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham's victory in the Makerfield by-election means he has to step down as Greater Manchester mayor Burnham has been mayor since the role was first created in 2017 and the race to become his successor will be fiercely contested by all involved But what is the role they will be fighting for? The role of mayor was created as part of a law passed in 2016, one of a number of big pieces of devolution legislation brought in by the Conservatives after taking power in 2010 In a 2012 referendum, Manchester rejected having a directly-elected city mayor, along with eight other major cities, but the decision to have a regional or metropolitan mayor was directly negotiated between the government and the 10 Greater Manchester councils Andy Burnham, who left Parliament to stand for the role, was chosen as Labour's candidate for the first mayoral election in 2017 and won, taking 63.4% of the vote

title: The Odyssey cast shown oldest book copy of Homer's epic poem

evidence_packet.title: The Odyssey cast shown oldest book copy of Homer's epic poem
evidence_packet.lead: The task of taking parts of the oldest book copy of The Odyssey to the US for the stars of Christopher Nolan's cinematic retelling of the epic to view was "like being on the set of Mission Impossible", the librarian who took it has said Part of a 1,700-year-old copy of Homer's po
evidence_packet.summary: The task of taking parts of the oldest book copy of The Odyssey to the US for the stars of Christopher Nolan's cinematic retelling of the epic to view was "like being on the set of Mission Impossible", the librarian who took it has said Part of a 1,700-year-old copy of Homer's po
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The task of taking parts of the oldest book copy of The Odyssey to the US for the stars of Christopher Nolan's cinematic retelling of the epic to view was "like being on the set of Mission Impossible", the librarian who took it has said Part of a 1,700-year-old copy of Homer's poem, kept at Manchester's John Rylands Library, was taken to New York in a bespoke case for the viewing Prof Christopher Pressler said it felt like a mission, as "we knew what was in this case but nobody else did", adding "It was a huge responsibility carrying something of global importance through JFK." He said it led to "some mind-blowing moments" for the cast, with Nolan being "very moved" by holding the fragments The fragments, written in ancient Greek by what was thought to be an Egyptian scribe and his teacher, are the oldest existing version of the poem arranged into a book Nolan's film, which was adapted from Homer's epic, stars Matt Damon as Odysseus, with Tom Holland playing his son, Telemachus, and Anne Hathaway as his wife, Penelope

title: Winter Hill still not fully recovered from moor fire eight years ago

evidence_packet.title: Winter Hill still not fully recovered from moor fire eight years ago
evidence_packet.lead: A moorland hit by a devastating wildfire eight years ago has still not fully recovered The summer 2018 blaze on Winter Hill near Bolton lasted 42 days and took about 100 firefighters to control and put out While some of the landscape has recovered, Alan Wright, from The Wildlife
evidence_packet.summary: A moorland hit by a devastating wildfire eight years ago has still not fully recovered The summer 2018 blaze on Winter Hill near Bolton lasted 42 days and took about 100 firefighters to control and put out While some of the landscape has recovered, Alan Wright, from The Wildlife
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A moorland hit by a devastating wildfire eight years ago has still not fully recovered The summer 2018 blaze on Winter Hill near Bolton lasted 42 days and took about 100 firefighters to control and put out While some of the landscape has recovered, Alan Wright, from The Wildlife Trust for Lancashire, Manchester and North Merseyside, said the impact was still visible He said: "The hill was completely black and this whole hill behind us was on fire. And it's not quite got the same kind of vegetation [now]." He added: "Any time there's a fire it will kill lots and lots of fledglings, it will kill lots of mammals, it will kill lots of insects, and then it will create areas which are just no-go areas for years to come because there are no food plants." Wright said that despite the long-term damage, a lot of work has been done to help re-grow plants and make the environment one in which wildlife could thrive again

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A large woodland and grass fire tackled overnight was probably caused by a disposable barbecue, the fire service has said Dozens of firefighters were called to the wildfire at Hacked Way Lane, near Macclesfield, Cheshire, just after 16:00 BST on Tuesday Ten fire engines and specialist units were there at its height with United Utilities helping with water drops by helicopter Cheshire Fire and Rescue service said a discarded barbecue was the "probable cause" and crews were still at the scene on Wednesday morning It was a reminder of the "devastating impact that careless behaviour can have on our countryside, particularly during periods of warm, dry weather", they said The fire service urged people to stay away from the area , saying visitors continued to arrive while emergency crews worked nearby

evidence_packet.title: Did Andy Burnham really fail to tackle homelessness as mayor?

evidence_packet.summary: Andy Burnham has twice pledged to end rough sleeping - when he was elected mayor of Greater Manchester and again in front of 10 Downing Street on Monday, in his first speech as prime minister His promise as mayor to end rough sleeping by 2020 appeared successful at first, with fi
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham has twice pledged to end rough sleeping - when he was elected mayor of Greater Manchester and again in front of 10 Downing Street on Monday, in his first speech as prime minister His promise as mayor to end rough sleeping by 2020 appeared successful at first, with figures falling from 268 people sleeping on the street in 2017, to 90 in 2021 But the dip also coincided with a national effort from councils to bring rough sleepers inside during the Covid-19 pandemic, and the figure has begun to rise again alongside hikes in the cost of living Some have criticised Burnham's failure to keep his promise as mayor, while others say 'the story in Manchester is positive' There were high-profile flashpoints in the city during his time as mayor, including the clearance of tents around St Peter's Square Last year, Manchester City Council said refugees were particularly drawn to Manchester as a "friendly global city", but many were falling into rough sleeping as support services grew overloaded with rising demand

title: Cries of 'coward' as family faces teenager's murderer in court

evidence_packet.title: Cries of 'coward' as family faces teenager's murderer in court
evidence_packet.lead: Courts Cries of 'coward' as family faces teenager's murderer in court Statements were read out on behalf of Devon Simmonds-Caines' loved ones View 3 Images Terrence King (left) and Devon Simmonds-Caines (right) (Image: Greater Manchester Police) News Amy Walker Court reporter 06
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Cries of 'coward' as family faces teenager's murderer in court Statements were read out on behalf of Devon Simmonds-Caines' loved ones View 3 Images Terrence King (left) and Devon Simmonds-Caines (right) (Image: Greater Manchester Police) News Amy Walker Court reporter 06
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Cries of 'coward' as family faces teenager's murderer in court Statements were read out on behalf of Devon Simmonds-Caines' loved ones View 3 Images Terrence King (left) and Devon Simmonds-Caines (right) (Image: Greater Manchester Police) News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:12, 24 Jul 2026 Updated 06:34, 24 Jul 2026 "You're a coward," a woman shouted from the public gallery at Minshull Street Crown Court as murderer Terrence King was led to the cells Earlier, the 60-year-old heard Devon Simmonds-Caines' loved ones speak of how he was beginning 'turn a corner in life'. That young life was snatched away on July 22 last year Devon was deliberately hit by King with his car. He was driving at almost double the speed limit. Devon, who was riding a stolen e-bike, suffered horrific injuries and sadly died at the scene on Rowrah Crescent in Langley, Middleton Following retrial earlier this month, King, of Castlerigg Drive, Middleton, was found guilty of murder As he was jailed for life, the court heard from members of Devon's family about the impact of losing him and how he was planning to create a life for himself despite his 'troubles'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Three injured and two arrested after BB gun fired at Jewish people in Salford Police say they are 'continuing to enhance our security in Jewish communities across Greater Manchester' News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 19:37, 23 Jul 2026 View Im Three people were injured when a BB was fired at members of the Jewish community in Salford. It happened on Leicester Road at around 10pm on Monday night (July 20) The three victims were 'shot with a BB gun from a passing vehicle', Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said. Thankfully, they suffered only 'minor' injuries Following 'extensive CCTV enquiries', two suspects were identified, who were then arrested on suspicion of aggravated common assault, GMP said No further details about the suspects, including their age or gender, have yet been released A force statement said: "Threats to our communities will not be tolerated and we're continuing to enhance our security in Jewish communities across Greater Manchester to help keep them safe on our streets."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Fire Service Moor fires update as fire crews 'move on' response after massive area devastated Fire chiefs have given the latest on their progress in Dovestone News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 19:13, 23 Jul 2026 View 4 Images The Do The fire services tackling huge moor fires in and around Greater Manchester say they are continuing to make progress Crews have been tackling the fire near Dovestone Reservoir, in Greenfield, Oldham, since last Saturday, with a nearby area of moorland at Swineshaw also alight. The operation to contain another moorland blaze at Tintwistle is also continuing, forcing the closure of the A628 Woodh In an update issued this evening (Thursday), Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) who are dealing with the blazes at Dovestone and Swineshaw, said crews 'continue to make steady progress.' In an updated statement they said: "The response has moved on this week from intensive firefighting to a longer-term containment phase, with crews focusing on extinguishing hotspots and preventing further spread "New fire breaks have been created across parts of the moorland and additional equipment is helping crews get water to some of the most remote areas of the incident ground."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester synagogue attack Revealed: The messages police missed that might have stopped the Heaton Park synagogue terrorist Jihad Al-Shamie shared a string of messages about jihad. But they weren't found until it was too late. View 8 Images GMP has a News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter and John Scheerhout Crime reporter 18:59, 23 Jul 2026 When police twice arrested Jihad Al-Shamie in the months before he carried out his terror attack at a Manchester synagogue, they seized his mobile phones But the devices weren't analysed and a series of incriminating, 'extremist mindset' messages he exchanged with a fellow jihadist remained undiscovered until it was too late. These were missed opportunities for which Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson has now apologised It meant Al-Shamie was released and was on bail when he carried out his deadly terror attack at Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation synagogue to mark Yom Kippur, the holiest day of the year for Jews on October 2 last year Sir Stephen said: "In conducting an internal review, it became apparent that GMP had seized Al-Shamie's mobile devices. The significance of the data contents of these devices was substantial in respect of evidencing an extremist mindset "Regrettably, I can confirm that the significance of the information stored on Al-Shamie's devices was not realised as they had not been examined before the attack took place on October 2."

evidence_packet.summary: Wigan First operator at 'giant cruise ship warehouse' in Tyldesley starts round-the-clock operations A logistics firm has been granted an interim licence to operate lorries round the clock at the controversial Astley Business Park Comments News Chris Logistics firm Whistl has sta
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan First operator at 'giant cruise ship warehouse' in Tyldesley starts round-the-clock operations A logistics firm has been granted an interim licence to operate lorries round the clock at the controversial Astley Business Park Comments News Chris Logistics firm Whistl has started round-the-clock operations at the controversial ‘cruise ship’ warehouse complex in Tyldesley The company began trading at unit 2 at the Astley Business Park on Monday (July 20) after being granted an interim licence by the traffic commissioner regarding heavy goods vehicle movements The firm previously agreed a 15-year lease for the unit with the intention of moving their local operation from the nearby Logistics North complex near Bolton. The now completed development has been dogged by controversy for more than a year since building work started Many residents, some of whom have gardens just 30 metres from the 350,000 sq ft logistics site, criticised the huge scale and appearance of the ‘towering warehouses’ Incidents of flooding on nearby paths and gardens have also occurred last winter with complaints that run off from the construction site was causing the issues

It comes as she refused to put a deadline on Andy Burnham's pledge to end rough sleeping Ashton-under-Lyne MP Ms Rayner was reappointed as Housing Secretary by Mr Burnham after he took over as Prime Minister on Monday. She previously held the role from July 2024 until September last year, when she resigned following an investigation into her tax affairs She faced a backlash after admitting she underpaid stamp duty on a flat in Hove, Sussex which she bought for £800,000 earlier that year The Stockport-born MP admitted she had failed to pay £40,000 in stamp duty as she claimed the property was her main home, rather than a second home. A report by ethics watchdog Sir Laurie Magnus found she had breached the ministerial code In May this year she said she had been 'exonerated' by HMRC who had 'cleared (her) of any wrongdoing.' She said she had taken 'reasonable care and acted in good faith, based on the expert advice I received, and HMRC has accepted this', adding she had paid 'every penny that I owed

title: Gun-wielding robber in 'spiral of chaos' had one question for police after Manchester Airport arrest

evidence_packet.title: Gun-wielding robber in 'spiral of chaos' had one question for police after Manchester Airport arrest
evidence_packet.lead: Courts Gun-wielding robber in 'spiral of chaos' had one question for police after Manchester Airport arrest Kaelun Howe was apprehended at Manchester Airport after a number of attacks Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 16:57, 23 Jul 2026 Updated A thug in a 'spiral of chaos'
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Gun-wielding robber in 'spiral of chaos' had one question for police after Manchester Airport arrest Kaelun Howe was apprehended at Manchester Airport after a number of attacks Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 16:57, 23 Jul 2026 Updated A thug in a 'spiral of chaos'
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Gun-wielding robber in 'spiral of chaos' had one question for police after Manchester Airport arrest Kaelun Howe was apprehended at Manchester Airport after a number of attacks Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 16:57, 23 Jul 2026 Updated A thug in a 'spiral of chaos' robbed a Salford bookies at 'gunpoint' before being eventually arrested at Manchester Airport. Manchester Crown Court heard how Kaelun Howe, 22, burgled - and attempted to burgle - numerous premises in the days leading up to the robbery at the bookie In April this year, he turned up at a man's house and pointed a gun at him through the peephole. "I'm going to shoot you," he said Later that afternoon, Howe forced his way into the William Hill at Salford precinct, armed with what appeared to be a gun, but turned out to be a BB gun. The cashier moved into a safe room behind glass before Howe shot at it He then climbed onto the counter and stole the contents of the till His terrifying attacks ended when he was arrested at Manchester Airport. Howe has now been jailed for six years and nine months for a string of burglary and robbery offences

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Reform bid to withdraw Wigan council from refugee resettlement schemes fails An hour long debate heard that newly elected Reform councillors had heard the same concerns about immigration from residents 'time and time again' Comments News Chris G A Reform bid to withdraw Wigan council from all discretionary refugee resettlement schemes has been rejected At a meeting of the full council, Pemberton representative Coun Simon Silcock, of Reform, brought forward a motion which claimed optional refugees’ schemes were ‘adding serious pressure on council housing, private rented accommodation, HMOs, schools, GP services and community coh The motion called on the council to withdraw from all discretionary refugee resettlement schemes and write to the Home Office, confirming that the borough will not accept further placements until housing, public services and community capacity are independently assessed and shown The motion added: “This will reaffirm that Wigan council will continue to provide lawful, fair and compassionate support to all residents already living in the borough, while prioritising transparency, and protecting the delivery of essential local services.” Coun Silcock said: “During the election we knocked on tens of thousands of doors across Wigan and Leigh and we heard the same concerns time and time again

They were spotted outside Heron House on Albert Square, the building currently occupied by GCHQ, which sits a stones' throw from M The building is set to be the interim home of Number 10 North, a move announced by Andy Burnham to 'rebalance' political power in Britain, out of which ministers are 'already' reportedly working, just two days on from the new MP's appointment

evidence_packet.lead: Courts Cries of 'coward' as family faces teenager's murderer in court Statements were read out on behalf of Devon Simmonds-Caines' loved ones View 3 Images Terrence King (left) and Devon Simmonds-Caines (right) (Image: Greater Manchester Police) News Amy Walker Court reporter 06
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Cries of 'coward' as family faces teenager's murderer in court Statements were read out on behalf of Devon Simmonds-Caines' loved ones View 3 Images Terrence King (left) and Devon Simmonds-Caines (right) (Image: Greater Manchester Police) News Amy Walker Court reporter 06
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Cries of 'coward' as family faces teenager's murderer in court Statements were read out on behalf of Devon Simmonds-Caines' loved ones View 3 Images Terrence King (left) and Devon Simmonds-Caines (right) (Image: Greater Manchester Police) News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:12, 24 Jul 2026 Updated 06:34, 24 Jul 2026 "You're a coward," a woman shouted from the public gallery at Minshull Street Crown Court as murderer Terrence King was led to the cells Earlier, the 60-year-old heard Devon Simmonds-Caines' loved ones speak of how he was beginning 'turn a corner in life'. That young life was snatched away on July 22 last year Devon was deliberately hit by King with his car. He was driving at almost double the speed limit. Devon, who was riding a stolen e-bike, suffered horrific injuries and sadly died at the scene on Rowrah Crescent in Langley, Middleton Following retrial earlier this month, King, of Castlerigg Drive, Middleton, was found guilty of murder As he was jailed for life, the court heard from members of Devon's family about the impact of losing him and how he was planning to create a life for himself despite his 'troubles'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Three injured and two arrested after BB gun fired at Jewish people in Salford Police say they are 'continuing to enhance our security in Jewish communities across Greater Manchester' News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 19:37, 23 Jul 2026 View Im Three people were injured when a BB was fired at members of the Jewish community in Salford. Thankfully, they suffered only 'minor' injuries Following 'extensive CCTV enquiries', two suspects were identified, who were then arrested on suspicion of aggravated common assault, GMP said No further details about the suspects, including their age or gender, have yet been released A force statement said: "Threats to our communities will not be tolerated and we're continuing to enhance our security in Jewish communities across Greater Manchester to help keep them safe on our streets."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Fire Service Moor fires update as fire crews 'move on' response after massive area devastated Fire chiefs have given the latest on their progress in Dovestone News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 19:13, 23 Jul 2026 View 4 Images The Do The fire services tackling huge moor fires in and around Greater Manchester say they are continuing to make progress Crews have been tackling the fire near Dovestone Reservoir, in Greenfield, Oldham, since last Saturday, with a nearby area of moorland at Swineshaw also alight. The operation to contain another moorland blaze at Tintwistle is also continuing, forcing the closure of the A628 Woodh In an update issued this evening (Thursday), Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) who are dealing with the blazes at Dovestone and Swineshaw, said crews 'continue to make steady progress.' In an updated statement they said: "The response has moved on this week from intensive firefighting to a longer-term containment phase, with crews focusing on extinguishing hotspots and preventing further spread "New fire breaks have been created across parts of the moorland and additional equipment is helping crews get water to some of the most remote areas of the incident ground."

title: Revealed: The messages police missed that might have stopped the Heaton Park synagogue terrorist

evidence_packet.lead: Manchester synagogue attack Revealed: The messages police missed that might have stopped the Heaton Park synagogue terrorist Jihad Al-Shamie shared a string of messages about jihad.
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester synagogue attack Revealed: The messages police missed that might have stopped the Heaton Park synagogue terrorist Jihad Al-Shamie shared a string of messages about jihad. But they weren't found until it was too late
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester synagogue attack Revealed: The messages police missed that might have stopped the Heaton Park synagogue terrorist Jihad Al-Shamie shared a string of messages about jihad. But they weren't found until it was too late. View 8 Images GMP has a News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter and John Scheerhout Crime reporter 18:59, 23 Jul 2026 When police twice arrested Jihad Al-Shamie in the months before he carried out his terror attack at a Manchester synagogue, they seized his mobile phones But the devices weren't analysed and a series of incriminating, 'extremist mindset' messages he exchanged with a fellow jihadist remained undiscovered until it was too late. These were missed opportunities for which Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson has now apologised It meant Al-Shamie was released and was on bail when he carried out his deadly terror attack at Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation synagogue to mark Yom Kippur, the holiest day of the year for Jews on October 2 last year Sir Stephen said: "In conducting an internal review, it became apparent that GMP had seized Al-Shamie's mobile devices. The significance of the data contents of these devices was substantial in respect of evidencing an extremist mindset "Regrettably, I can confirm that the significance of the information stored on Al-Shamie's devices was not realised as they had not been examined before the attack took place on October 2."

And whole purpose of No 10 North is to put more power into every postcode in the land, including the postcodes of Harlow." The former mayor of Greater Manchester added: "How do we get power out of Whitehall and Westminster, into the hands of people at a local level, so that they can make a difference and turn things around?” It comes a day after police officers were seen guarding the entrance of the interim No 10 North site in Manchester city centre on Wednesday, July 22. That young life was snatched away on July 22 last year Devon was deliberately hit by King with his car. He was driving at almost double the speed limit. Devon, who was riding a stolen e-bike, suffered horrific injuries and sadly died at the scene on Rowrah Crescent in Langley, Middleton Following retrial earlier this month, King, of Castlerigg Drive, Middleton, was found guilty of murder As he was jailed for life, the court heard from members of Devon's family about the impact of losing him and how he was planning to create a life for himself despite his 'troubles'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Andy Burnham declares Manchester's Number 10 North open as Prime Minister to visit on Friday Downing Street say the new Prime Minister will spend time there each week and that other cabinet ministers will work there on a 'regular basis' C Andy Burnham says 'the days of Whitehall resisting devolution are over' as he prepares to spend his first day working at No 10 North The Prime Minister will 'throw open the doors' to the newly-formed branch of Downing Street, to be based in Manchester, tomorrow (Friday, July 24) his office said He is to spend the end of his first working week in office at the new hub where he will chair the first meeting of the revived National Economic Council Currently operating from Heron House, facing Albert Square in Manchester city centre, Downing Street says No 10 North will 'he levers of local economic growth and devolution together under one roof for the first time' and act as a 'new situation room for growth.' evidence_packet.title: Gun-wielding robber in 'spiral of chaos' had one question for police after Manchester Airport arrest
evidence_packet.lead: Courts Gun-wielding robber in 'spiral of chaos' had one question for police after Manchester Airport arrest Kaelun Howe was apprehended at Manchester Airport after a number of attacks Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 16:57, 23 Jul 2026 Updated A thug in a 'spiral of chaos'
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Gun-wielding robber in 'spiral of chaos' had one question for police after Manchester Airport arrest Kaelun Howe was apprehended at Manchester Airport after a number of attacks Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 16:57, 23 Jul 2026 Updated A thug in a 'spiral of chaos'
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Gun-wielding robber in 'spiral of chaos' had one question for police after Manchester Airport arrest Kaelun Howe was apprehended at Manchester Airport after a number of attacks Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 16:57, 23 Jul 2026 Updated A thug in a 'spiral of chaos' robbed a Salford bookies at 'gunpoint' before being eventually arrested at Manchester Airport. Manchester Crown Court heard how Kaelun Howe, 22, burgled - and attempted to burgle - numerous premises in the days leading up to the robbery at the bookie In April this year, he turned up at a man's house and pointed a gun at him through the peephole. "I'm going to shoot you," he said Later that afternoon, Howe forced his way into the William Hill at Salford precinct, armed with what appeared to be a gun, but turned out to be a BB gun. The cashier moved into a safe room behind glass before Howe shot at it He then climbed onto the counter and stole the contents of the till His terrifying attacks ended when he was arrested at Manchester Airport. Howe has now been jailed for six years and nine months for a string of burglary and robbery offences

evidence_packet.summary: Salford Three injured and two arrested after BB gun fired at Jewish people in Salford Police say they are 'continuing to enhance our security in Jewish communities across Greater Manchester' News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 19:37, 23 Jul 2026 View Im Three people were injured wh
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Three injured and two arrested after BB gun fired at Jewish people in Salford Police say they are 'continuing to enhance our security in Jewish communities across Greater Manchester' News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 19:37, 23 Jul 2026 View Im Three people were injured when a BB was fired at members of the Jewish community in Salford. It happened on Leicester Road at around 10pm on Monday night (July 20) The three victims were 'shot with a BB gun from a passing vehicle', Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said. Thankfully, they suffered only 'minor' injuries Following 'extensive CCTV enquiries', two suspects were identified, who were then arrested on suspicion of aggravated common assault, GMP said No further details about the suspects, including their age or gender, have yet been released A force statement said: "Threats to our communities will not be tolerated and we're continuing to enhance our security in Jewish communities across Greater Manchester to help keep them safe on our streets."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Fire Service Moor fires update as fire crews 'move on' response after massive area devastated Fire chiefs have given the latest on their progress in Dovestone News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 19:13, 23 Jul 2026 View 4 Images The Do The fire services tackling huge moor fires in and around Greater Manchester say they are continuing to make progress Crews have been tackling the fire near Dovestone Reservoir, in Greenfield, Oldham, since last Saturday, with a nearby area of moorland at Swineshaw also alight. The operation to contain another moorland blaze at Tintwistle is also continuing, forcing the closure of the A628 Woodh In an update issued this evening (Thursday), Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) who are dealing with the blazes at Dovestone and Swineshaw, said crews 'continue to make steady progress.' In an updated statement they said: "The response has moved on this week from intensive firefighting to a longer-term containment phase, with crews focusing on extinguishing hotspots and preventing further spread "New fire breaks have been created across parts of the moorland and additional equipment is helping crews get water to some of the most remote areas of the incident ground."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester synagogue attack Revealed: The messages police missed that might have stopped the Heaton Park synagogue terrorist Jihad Al-Shamie shared a string of messages about jihad. But they weren't found until it was too late. View 8 Images GMP has a News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter and John Scheerhout Crime reporter 18:59, 23 Jul 2026 When police twice arrested Jihad Al-Shamie in the months before he carried out his terror attack at a Manchester synagogue, they seized his mobile phones But the devices weren't analysed and a series of incriminating, 'extremist mindset' messages he exchanged with a fellow jihadist remained undiscovered until it was too late. These were missed opportunities for which Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson has now apologised It meant Al-Shamie was released and was on bail when he carried out his deadly terror attack at Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation synagogue to mark Yom Kippur, the holiest day of the year for Jews on October 2 last year Sir Stephen said: "In conducting an internal review, it became apparent that GMP had seized Al-Shamie's mobile devices. The significance of the data contents of these devices was substantial in respect of evidencing an extremist mindset "Regrettably, I can confirm that the significance of the information stored on Al-Shamie's devices was not realised as they had not been examined before the attack took place on October 2."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Killer driver who mowed down teenager 'in unlawful act of retribution' jailed for life 'An act of unlawful private retribution' Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 13:21, 23 Jul 2026 Updated 15:42, 23 Jul 2026 View 4 Images Terrence King, l A killer driver who mowed down a teenager in 'an unlawful act of retribution' has been jailed for life Terrence King, 60, deliberately ploughed into 15-year-old with his car, driving at almost double the speed limit. Devon Simmonds-Caines, who was riding a stolen e-bike, suffered catastrophic injuries and sadly died at the scene on Rowrah Crescent in Langley, Middleton on July 22, At trial, King claimed that he only wanted to ‘block in’ the bike to stop it, and that he had no intention of harming Devon. King first stood trial in January, when jurors were deadlocked and could not agree on a verdict. In the aftermath of the jury being discharged, King pleade Following a retrial earlier this month, King was found guilty of murder. Today, July 23, King was jailed for life to serve a minimum of 16 years and one day A judge told him: "This was an act of unlawful private retribution. The robbery of the bike was wrong, but it did not entitle you to harm anyone. The law does not permit anger, panic or misguided loyalty to be turned into violence."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Friday 19 June 2026 at 1:43pm Andy Burnham has been mayor of Greater Manchester for almost a decade. Credit: PA Images Andy Burnham’s historic victory in the Makerfield by-election sets off a rapid chain reaction for both Greater Manchester and the wider UK political landscape A metro mayor cannot simultaneously serve as an MP, a clear legal and electoral process is now underway to find someone new to take on the role Andy Burnham has won a seat as an MP - but can he still be the Mayor of Greater Manchester? No. Andy Burnham cannot be mayor and a member of parliament. He had seven days - from the moment of his election - to resign from the post which he has held for almost a decade He handed in his resignation on 19 June - triggering the process of the by-election Burnham cannot do both jobs because the Mayor of Greater Manchester holds Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC) powers and UK law strictly dictates that the office holder cannot simultaneously serve as an MP

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mohammad Bashir, 31, drove his friend Jihad Al-Shamie on a 10-hour round trip to conduct hostile reconnaissance at the UK's Defence Academy in Shrivenham, Oxfordshire, on 14 August 2025 Weeks after that journey, Al-Shamie, 35, was shot dead by police after carrying out the Heaton Park Synagogue attack, in which two Jewish men were killed Bashir, from Cheetham Hill, was sentenced at Manchester Crown Court after pleading guilty to one count of preparing an act of terrorism Sentencing Bashir, Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb told him that by August last year he had become a "firmly committed jihadist" He and Al-Shamie were "equally engaged" in planning an attack on a British military target "in which you and he expected to kill and be killed", she said She rejected his claim to a probation officer that he no longer held extremist views and regretted his actions

title: Police failed to check Manchester synagogue attacker's phones despite arrests

evidence_packet.title: Police failed to check Manchester synagogue attacker's phones despite arrests
evidence_packet.lead: Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, was on bail for an alleged rape when he carried out the attack on Heaton Park Synagogue in Crumpsall on 2 October 2025, in which two Jewish men were killed His devices, which contained evidence of his extreme views, were seized after he was arrested in Februa
evidence_packet.summary: Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, was on bail for an alleged rape when he carried out the attack on Heaton Park Synagogue in Crumpsall on 2 October 2025, in which two Jewish men were killed His devices, which contained evidence of his extreme views, were seized after he was arrested in Februa
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, was on bail for an alleged rape when he carried out the attack on Heaton Park Synagogue in Crumpsall on 2 October 2025, in which two Jewish men were killed His devices, which contained evidence of his extreme views, were seized after he was arrested in February and September but not analysed Greater Manchester Police Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson said he was "deeply sorry", conceding that "the information contained within these devices would have inspired further investigative action" Sir Stephen said the end of legal proceedings against Mohammad Bashir, who has been jailed for life with a minimum term of 17 years for plotting a separate attack with Al-Shamie, meant rules around sharing information about a live criminal case had been lifted He said: "In conducting an internal review, it became apparent that GMP had seized Al-Shamie's mobile devices, at the point of each arrest "The significance of the data contents of these devices was substantial in respect of evidencing an extremist mindset

title: Winter Hill still not fully recovered from moor fire eight years ago

evidence_packet.title: Winter Hill still not fully recovered from moor fire eight years ago
evidence_packet.lead: The summer 2018 blaze on Winter Hill near Bolton lasted 42 days and took about 100 firefighters to control and put out While some of the landscape has recovered, Alan Wright, from The Wildlife Trust for Lancashire, Manchester and North Merseyside, said the impact was still visibl
evidence_packet.summary: The summer 2018 blaze on Winter Hill near Bolton lasted 42 days and took about 100 firefighters to control and put out While some of the landscape has recovered, Alan Wright, from The Wildlife Trust for Lancashire, Manchester and North Merseyside, said the impact was still visibl
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The summer 2018 blaze on Winter Hill near Bolton lasted 42 days and took about 100 firefighters to control and put out While some of the landscape has recovered, Alan Wright, from The Wildlife Trust for Lancashire, Manchester and North Merseyside, said the impact was still visible He said: "The hill was completely black and this whole hill behind us was on fire. And it's not quite got the same kind of vegetation [now]." He added: "Any time there's a fire it will kill lots and lots of fledglings, it will kill lots of mammals, it will kill lots of insects, and then it will create areas which are just no-go areas for years to come because there are no food plants." Wright said that despite the long-term damage, a lot of work has been done to help re-grow plants and make the environment one in which wildlife could thrive again "A lot of it is down to making sure the land is wet, and kind of creating areas which are wet, and looking after areas and making sure that the right type of vegetation is growing," he added

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Borough is seeing a positive decline in the number of young people smoking and regularly vaping, according to a recent Trading Standards survey Following national concerns about youth smoking and vaping, Wigan Council has made it a priority to reduce these figures locally and protect the health of our children and young people With more than 1,000 school children aged 14-17 included in the Trading Standards survey, the findings show the number of young people who have tried vaping dropped from around 44 per cent in 2023 to 18 per cent in 2026 The survey, carried out between November 2025 and February 2026, also highlights that smoking is at an all-time low, with around 97 per cent reporting to have never tried smoking Councillor Keith Cunliffe, Deputy Leader of Wigan Council and cabinet portfolio holder for adult social care and health, said: “I’m really pleased to see smoking and vaping rates among young people in Wigan Borough continuing to fall “Reducing tobacco and nicotine use among young people is one of the most effective ways to prevent long-term ill health and reduce health inequalities in our communities

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: It might have first made headlines because of Rio the parrot, but now Gardens’ controversial feathered resident has been rehomed, the spotlight is firmly back where it belongs – on the food Gardens is a striking new waterside restaurant and lounge overlooking the River Irwell, with enormous windows taking in views of the water and Manchester Cathedral Greater Manchester has historically not been very good about making the most of its waterways, with areas like Ancoats Marina and Salford Quays now leading a new charge, so it’s refreshing to see somewhere making the most of the Irwell – even if there’s still more chance of seein With its towering ceilings and stylish interiors, Gardens has quickly become one of Salford’s most eye-catching new openings, promising hearty Mediterranean grills, shisha, and great mocktails And now there’s another reason to visit, as the venue has launched a brand new Lebanese-inspired brunch menu Expect authentic dishes including fluffy omelettes, hearty foul (slow-cooked fava beans), prawn fatteh (layers of crisp pitta, tahini yoghurt, chickpeas, and prawns), shakshuka, and fresh halloumi tomato salad, alongside plenty of other Mediterranean favourites

evidence_packet.title: Fairfield Social Club
evidence_packet.lead: Fancy a space to connect with the community away from Canal Street?
evidence_packet.summary: Fancy a space to connect with the community away from Canal Street? Kiki Family Social is a relaxed, grassroots meet-up with no rigid expectations, pressure, or hierarchy
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fancy a space to connect with the community away from Canal Street? Kiki Family Social is a relaxed, grassroots meet-up with no rigid expectations, pressure, or hierarchy. The space is shaped by the people who come along — everyone helps make it what it is We meet every Thursday, and there’s always space at the table whether you’re new to Manchester or just dipping your toe into social meet-ups You’ll usually find a mix of familiar faces and new ones each week. We typically gather at a reserved table inside with pride flags, and there’s often a table outside too. On busy nights we’ll make sure flags are on the outside table as well. If you’re unsure where we are, just a 📅 Every Thursday, 7:30pm (You’re welcome to arrive earlier or later) 🍻 This isn’t a sober event, but there’s no pressure to drink. The bar offers zero-alcohol options as well as tea and coffee

We typically gather at a reserved table inside with pride flags, and there’s often a table outside too. On busy nights we’ll make sure flags are on the outside table as well. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale | Bolton Sunday Car Boot Sale | Times, Prices & Info Skip to content 210+ UK car boot sales — find one near you this weekend Type your postcode or town to find sales near you Search car boot sales About This Car Boot Sale Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. Last confirmed open: 8 June 2026. evidence_packet.lead: JJ Gabriel, 15, gets senior Man Utd call-up
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester United reporter in Trondheim Published 23 July 2026 Fifteen-year-old forward JJ Gabriel has been named in Manchester United 's senior squad for the first time for Friday's friendly against Rosenborg The youngster, who was the Under-18 Premier League player of the seaso
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester United reporter in Trondheim Published 23 July 2026 Fifteen-year-old forward JJ Gabriel has been named in Manchester United 's senior squad for the first time for Friday's friendly against Rosenborg The youngster, who was the Under-18 Premier League player of the season last term despite only being 14 when the campaign began, is part of Michael Carrick's 25-man travelling party for the pre-season friendly in Trondheim Gabriel, who does not turn 16 until October, joins the squad that was beaten 1-0 by Wrexham in Finland last week, with striker Ethan Wheatley dropping out It means there is no place for 18-year-old Tynan Thompson, who has joined from Tottenham in an £8m deal. Striker Benjamin Sesko, goalkeeper Karl Darlow and defender Matthijs de Ligt are all ruled out by injury It had been expected Gabriel would play some part in United's pre-season this summer given the progress the Londoner has made through the club's youth system But should the winger feature in Norway to make his first senior appearance for the club, it will be the latest milestone in the teenager's career

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC How Manchester United should line up vs Rosenborg in second pre-season friendly Man United are in Norway today as they prepare to take on Rosenborg in their second pre-season fixture. Comments Sport opinion Steven Railston Manchester United cor Manchester United are preparing for their second pre-season fixture of the summer against Rosenborg in Trondheim, Norway. Exciting academy star JJ Gabriel could make his maiden appearance for the first team today after being included in the travelling squad Gabriel would have been in contention to face Wrexham last week but his late return to training scuppered those plans. Young striker Ethan Wheatley misses out on this travelling squad to make room for Gabriel. Otherwise, it is an identical 25-man squad that lost in Helsinki Karl Darlow continues his recovery at Carrington. Meanwhile, Benjamin Sesko's shin injury means he misses out on this trip again. Take a look at how our United writers think the Reds should line up Carrick showed his hand last week by picking a strong team in the first half and then ringing the changes after the break. I'd keep the pattern reasonably similar this half, with a couple of changes One of them is moving Yoro to centre-back alongside Maguire . There has to be a chance that this is the partnership that begins the Premier League season, so let's see them together now

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United Transfer News Man United could raise £90m this summer with Marcus Rashford and Joshua Zirkzee decisions Manchester United will need to raise funds to continue their summer spending Comments Sport Tom Victor 04:30, 24 Jul 2026 View 3 Images Marcus After spending £80million in the early part of the transfer window, Manchester United will need to be smart during the remainder of the summer. Further recruits will be needed but there's also a chance to raise funds with some sales United have already got some big wages off the books. Casemiro and Jadon Sancho both left upon the expiry of their contracts, Rasmus Hojlund joined Napoli permanently, and Andre Onana will have most of his salary covered by Trabzonspor during his loan After wrapping up deals for new midfielders Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, one more central midfielder may well be required. Michael Carrick will also want reinforcements up front to deal with the extra matches in the schedule compared to last season A summer exit for Manuel Ugarte may need to be parked after the Uruguayan picked up an injury at the World Cup but there are still other ways to raise money. Here, we've taken a look at some players who can help bring in those funds For a while it looked as though United were set to lose Rashford for just £26million after a clause was inserted into his Barcelona loan. However, the Catalan club allowed it to expire after moving for Anthony Gordon earlier in the window

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester City FC Enzo Maresca must brace himself for major Man City transfer test Manchester City will unveil Enzo Maresca to the media on Friday and the new boss already has some transfer questions to answer. Comments Sport opinion Jack Flintham Sport Central Au Taking over from Pep Guardiola was always going to be a daunting task. Throughout his Manchester City tenure, Enzo Maresca will naturally be compared to Guardiola, with each decision analysed closely. It's an unenviable challenge One major test of his decision-making is now looming large after developments on Thursday. Leeds have approached City for their goalkeeper James Trafford . This won't come as a surprise to Maresca . Trafford was the best second-choice goalkeeper in the league last season His performances in the FA Cup and Carabao Cup helped City win both domestic trophies. It was a dream scenario for Guardiola. Gianluigi Donnarumma performed well in the Premier League and Champions League , while Trafford held down the fort in his absence. City lost very little w Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN! However, it was also unsustainable. Trafford was never going to accept being a second choice. At 23, he needs regular first-team football. 17 appearances may have been enough to get him into the World Cup squad, but it was certainly not enough to keep him happy

Luckily, we’ve just spotted a way to pick up Man City’s Puma FtblCulture Track Jacket for less than 90p This £75 jacket has plummeted to £16 in Kitbag’s clearance sales, but savvy shoppers can get it for pennies. Man City fans can get this cheaper price if they set up a free TopCashback account , which comes with a £15 welcome bonus when spending £15 or more It also pays cashback on Kitbag orders, which means the jacket effectively drops to 87p after cashback, saving a whopping £74.13 or roughly 99% from the original price. Only new TopCashback members can claim this deal, but existing members can still secure a slightly cheaper pric Both options also include free delivery when using the code DEAL at checkout. A similar deal is available at rival retailer Fanatics , where the same jacket also costs £16 (was £75) The Man City FtblCulture Jacket is said to be designed for ‘style and comfort’, coming in City blue with a darker navy blue across the shoulders and top chest and zipper pockets on each side. evidence_packet.evidence_text: 17 октября 2026 года в Brixton Jamm состоится концерт Андрея Кравченко в Лондоне Андрей Кравченко покорил сердца тысяч слушателей благодаря своему уникальному голосу, харизме и способности превращать личные истории в песни, близкие каждому. В его творчестве смешиваются романтическая лирика, современное эстрадное звучание и проникновенная искренность После серии аншлаговых выступлений на самых престижных сценах Украины, среди которых Жовтневый Дворец и Дворец “Украина”, певец продолжает свое концертное путешествие и приглашает поклонников на особую встречу в Лондоне Концерты Андрея Кравченко известны своей теплой атмосферой: здесь нет дистанции между сценой и залом, ведь каждое выступление превращается в откровенный разговор на языке музыки. Гостей ждут любимые хиты, живой звук, море эмоций и моменты, которые захочется сохранить в памяти над Важной частью творческой миссии артиста остается поддержка Украины — часть средств от концерта будет передана на помощь ВСУ! Подарите себе вечер настоящей романтики, красивой музыки и искренних чувств вместе с Андреем Кравченко

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rudy’s Pizza Napoletana has confirmed it will be bringing its relaxed dining experience and renowned Neapolitan pizzas to Salford for the first time, with a new restaurant opening in Monton village this autumn. To celebrate, the pizzeria is giving away 3,000 pizzas on the house a The new pizzeria, located at 237-239 Monton Road , will transform the former Bennetts Furnishers store that has been vacant since 2022, with work now officially underway. The spacious venue will mark Rudy’s 41st restaurant to date Since launching in Manchester’s Ancoats in 2015, Rudy’s has grown into one of the UK’s most loved pizzerias, celebrated for its light, double fermented dough and unwavering dedication to true Neopolitan craft Testament to its authenticity, Rudy’s is the largest organisation in the world to be accredited by the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana (AVPN), the international body that protects and promotes traditional Neapolitan pizza making Rudy’s has also been recognised among the World’s 50 Best Pizzeria, ranking 23rd globally for 2025. Each pizza, from the classic Margherita to the fiery Calabrese, is made to AVPN standards using traditional techniques and ingredients sourced directly from Italy To claim one of 3,000 complimentary pizzas, Monton locals can sign up via this link , where they will be able to choose from Rudy’s favourites such as its Cinghiale , Margherita Con Bufala, and Triple Pepperoni to enjoy at the new opening this summer
